questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities, living in a new country and engaging actively in the communities, exploring new cultures.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was available for the most part

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was the possibility to receive a guided tour of the university, but this wasn't provided by the university itself. We registered our arrival with our Erasmus coordinator and received our student card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There a different platforms and lots of possibilities, but it is expensive. I used SpotAHome. You pay a fee for the long term rental, but they assist you with any issues and will make sure that you receive the deposit upon returning home, which is very reassuring.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are many great places to live around Milan, however it is more expensive than the accommodations provided by the university. Make sure to look for accommodation a couple of months in advance, as there is a great demand for housing in Milan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We registered our arrival with the Erasmus coordinator and received our student card subsequently.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The guidance in the e-mail, as to the location of the office and the necessary printed documents and the rest was self-explanatory.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We could register for all classes and it was easy to switch subjects during the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The necessary information is provided in the e-mail, but make sure to register as soon as possible, as the registration date is relevant for the Erasmus grant.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were of varying degrees. Some were fairly easy, as they contained some repetition of classes that I had already had previously at my host institution. Some were harder, but in general the academic level (requirements to receive good grades) is not incredibly demanding. The courses are also different depending on whether it is focused more on political discussion or legal analysis.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UCPH is more case-based and focuses more on the domestic law of our country. The international courses at UNIMI are often focused on comparisons between different law systems in different countries or regions within a given area of law. the type of teaching varies, but generally the students are included less in discussion etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative Contract Law
Comparative Industrial Relations Systems 
Labour Law and Environmental Sustainability 
International Criminal Law
Transnational Commercial Litigation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend these courses for students interested in labour law:
Comparative Industrial Relations Systems 
Labour Law and Environmental Sustainability 

The teacher has both courses. He is very engaged and includes the students in interesting discussions/dilemmas. The teacher is also very good at clarifying information about the exam and examination methods, which gives clarity as to the requirements for the exam. Overall a great experience. 

Comparative Contract Law and International Criminal Law is also recommendable.

Transnational Commercial Litigation is an interesting subject, but the teaching method lacks innovation and inclusion of the students and there is not enough information about the exam.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus Student Network offers a lot of different activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Touring the city or joining social activities, especially night-life activities for students, where you can get to now other international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go visit some of the cities around Milan, visit one of the many museums in the city or try interesting restaurants or bars.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. They are very accepting of internatonal students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendliness, happiness, the food and drinks, and the rich culture that evolves around these foods. I liked the laid-back approach to daily life, businessmen and -women taking a long lunch break during workdays to talk and recharge for the rest of the day. Italians are a very talkative people and the like to go out to eat and drink. Very charming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Use your time smartly, be active. Explore Milan, but also take your time to plan trips outside of Milan. I regretted not travelling more to other parts of Italy, as the travelling opportunities (train, bus, plane) are great and cheap. The university is located very centrally, so also make sure to check out the gems hidden around the outer skirts of Milan.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the teachers or the Erasmus coordinator if you have any doubts or practical questions, they will happily answer them.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finding new friends, trying a new school systems, living in another country and in another culture, and travelling, both alone and with friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not spending money.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
